A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AAPO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite additions, relocation, and reformatting.

before.justification: Section 6, Tables 1–2, and the training plots report original AAPO experiments and clipping ablations on Qwen-family models.

after.justification: v2 retains the original Qwen experiments and adds original Llama comparisons and training-loss statistics in Section 6 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The advantage-weighted cross-entropy objective, clipped policy–reference reward difference, dual-group sampling, and frozen reference model remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves from Section 4 to Appendix A without a substantive procedural revision.

E1.justification: The five evaluation benchmarks and Qwen training datasets are retained. Appendix C.2 names simplelr_able_level3to5 for the added Llama experiments, whereas Qwen uses simplelr_qwen_level3to5. The PDFs do not establish whether these contain different data or whether the new identifier is a naming error; adding model families alone does not establish new task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes rStar-Math-7B. Appendix D adds GRPO to the dedicated loss comparison previously limited to AAPO and GPG, although GRPO already participated in other comparisons. The new Llama experiments use the existing GRPO/GPG comparison algorithms.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and 3B-Instruct experiments, with their own training configurations and a vLLM/SimpleRL evaluation procedure. It also revises the stated Qwen-7B batching from batch size 16 to per-device batch size 8 with four accumulation steps. This is a reported setting revision, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The clipping ablations and existing reward, response-length, and AAPO/GPG loss analyses remain. Section 6.3 newly quantifies training stability through loss variances, and Appendix D adds an AAPO-versus-GRPO loss plot.

E5.justification: v2 first reports training-loss variances: 3.6e-4 for AAPO, 3.9e-4 for GPG, and 3.53e-3 for GRPO. These summarize within-training variability rather than uncertainty across independent runs. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Llama results: AAPO averages 11.5 and 18.8 for 1B and 3B, versus GPG's 9.0 and 16.2. Both Qwen base-model rows receive replacement scores marked as reproduced, while AAPO's Qwen averages remain 56.7 and 52.4. Appendix E adds source-reported baseline results under their original settings. The new Qwen-7B base average is printed as 39.6, although its five scores average 29.6.

T1.justification: v2 adds stability and convergence theorems with substantial proofs in Appendix B, introducing bounded-gradient, variance-floor, smoothness, stochastic-gradient, and step-size assumptions. It also replaces v1's piecewise clipped GRPO gradient in Equations 8–9 with the simpler expression in v2 Equation 8.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion extend the performance claim to multiple model series, supported by the added Llama experiments. The central contribution—using advantage momentum to address inefficient group-relative optimization—remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds a caveat that evaluation results can depend on computational device type and interprets the new loss statistics as stability evidence. It removes v1's explicit limitation concerning substantial computational resources and long training time. Most mechanism and generalization interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies per-device batching and four gradient-accumulation steps for Qwen experiments. It also documents Llama reward weights, group and batch sizes, A800 hardware, absence of an extra training system prompt, and evaluation software. These expand reproducibility information without establishing reruns.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shannon (1948) and Robbins and Siegmund (1971) for the new proofs and removes the rStar-Math reference. The related-work narrative and positioning against GRPO/GPG remain largely unchanged; most other reference revisions are publication or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order are retained. v2 makes localized wording corrections, changes the title to 'Enhancing,' updates authorship and affiliation text, moves Algorithm 1 to an appendix, and reorganizes the appendices around the added material.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and substantially restructures displays. Table 1 expands into four model groups, Table 3 is added, the clipping chart becomes a much smaller unnumbered plot, prompt figures become unnumbered boxes, and the appendix loss figure becomes a redrawn two-panel comparison. The main training curves are retained.

improvement.justification: The Llama comparisons address v1's reliance on Qwen-family evidence, and the expanded setup details improve reproducibility, providing a limited net gain. This gain is tempered by the incorrect Table 1 average, removal of the compute/time limitation, and new convergence arguments whose positive-variance and independent-sampling assumptions are not established for the described training procedure. The unchanged method and Qwen results do not support treating the revision as a major overall improvement.
